label: Prophet-OAME-MBD
elements: Li, Be, B, C, Na, Mg, Al, Si, P, S
notes: Prophet-V1-MBD, the Matbench Discovery submission checkpoint (F1 0.9275, kappa_SRME 0.0648): 62.3M parameters, 10 layers, lmax 4, nested cutoffs 3/7 A, thermal-conductivity fine-tuned.  Multi-Cutoff Spectral Decomposition recombines nested cutoff scales linearly, which the report claims keeps E(3) equivariance exact and the energy twice continuously differentiable -- the equivariance and conservativity probes test exactly that claim.  Weights are CC-BY-4.0 and ungated; the checkpoint is staged by hand next to the others because KairosCalculator takes a filesystem path, not a hub id (hf download kairosmaterial/prophet prophet-oame-mbd.pt).  The magnetic sibling Prophet-V1-Mag ships in the same package behind prophet_spin.SpinCalculator and is not certified here: it needs an explicit magnetic state as input.
training_set_note: Three training stages, per the technical report: OMat24 and the composition-complete ELEMENTA corpus, then MPtrj and sAlex, then the perturbed-structure subset ELEMENTA Vib.  The ELEMENTA Vib count is the source's own approximate ~8M, and it publishes no material count, so n_training_materials is null for this row while n_training_structures is a sum that includes an approximate term.

datasets.label: OMat24
datasets.notes: Open Materials 2024 (Meta FAIR): >100M structures from perturbing Alexandria structures.

datasets.label: ELEMENTA
datasets.notes: Kairos Materials' composition-complete first-principles corpus (VASP, PBE+U, PBE pseudopotentials).

datasets.label: MPtrj
datasets.notes: Materials Project relaxation trajectories, cleaned and subsampled to about every 10th ionic step; created for CHGNet.

datasets.label: sAlex
datasets.notes: Alexandria subsampled by FAIR, filtered to remove prototype overlap with the Matbench Discovery WBM test set.

datasets.label: ELEMENTA Vib
datasets.notes: ELEMENTA expansion set: perturbed structures probing local vibrational environments, the corpus Prophet's third training stage uses.
